title: Efficacy of low-dose atropine to reduce myopia progression among Indian children

license.statement: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 License)

groups.description: single open-label group of 60 children treated with 0.01% atropine eye drops for 1 year at a tertiary eye care centre in south India; age not reported

series.notes: right eyes (OD) only; mean +/- SD, the baseline cell also prints the range; '1 year follow-up' = 12 months; biometry device not stated; units not stated in the table, the text gives axial increases in mm

exclusions.reason: right and left eyes of the same children are tabulated separately; only right eyes are extracted (protocol inclusion 7)

exclusions.what: Table 1 columns C2-C3 (spherical equivalent and rate of myopia progression)

exclusions.reason: ranges are not admissible as values; only the leading mean is read

notes: Letter to the editor reporting an open trial of 0.01% atropine for 1 year in 60 children recruited at a tertiary eye care centre in south India; no comparison group.
The letter classifies 10 of the 60 children as non-responders by refractive progression; Table 1 covers all 60 children, so the extracted set is not selected by outcome.
Mean age, biometry device and dropouts are not reported; all 60 children are described at 1 year.
Units: the table does not print units; the text reports axial-length increases in millimetres, so millimetres are assumed.
The mean axial increases quoted in the text do not equal the differences of the tabulated means; the tabulated means are cited.
Spherical equivalent at baseline and 1 year and the rate of myopia progression are tabulated and not extracted.
